primary_work.title: Synthetic Potential Outcomes and Causal Mixture Identifiability

decision: NARROWED BEYOND CAUSAL-RESPONSE MIXTURE IDENTIFIABILITY — NOT ADOPTED
prior_art_boundary: grouping latent populations by intervention response rather than covariate similarity is prior art
identifying ATEs and finite mixtures of treatment effects from observable proxy moments is prior art
recovering distinct causal-response components and their probabilities without full latent mixture recovery is prior art
higher-order multilinear-moment recovery of treatment-effect mixtures is prior art
recovery of a causal-response partition does not imply discovery of raw-language equivalence, semantic target identity, or denotation
assumptions: Z conditionally independent of Y given T and U
for MTE identification X conditionally independent of Y and T given U
observable moment matrices M[Z,X|T=t] full rank for both treatment values
distinct treatment-response values for finite moment-mixture recovery
counterexample: Two models can share the complete observable treatment, outcome, proxy, and language distributions; every SPO multilinear moment; all response moments; ATE; identified MTE support and weights after merging equal response values; conditional-independence and rank conditions; next-state prediction; action accuracy; task success; and language-shuffle gaps, while one treats two utterances as synonyms denoting one semantic target and the other treats them as distinct classes denoting two semantic targets that are response-aliased under every available intervention and outcome. Even with distinct responses, simultaneous permutation of response-component labels, target labels, utterance classes, and denotation preserves all observables. Therefore causal-response mixture identification does not jointly identify raw-language equivalence, the semantic latent intervention-target partition, or denotation.
official_code_status: paper-specific official code verified and exact commit pinned; README documents Python 3.9 compatibility, setup script, ATE and MTE replication commands, and an estimated 1–2 minute runtime; immutable dependency lock, canonical three-seed manifest, checksum bundle, raw-result provenance, model-size, RSS, and formal wall-time contract are not established
